_readme: SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for the request/response shapes the dashboard and the backend
must agree on. It exists because five production-breaking bugs shipped at once, all of
the same class: the two repos disagreed about a field name or a payload shape while 275
backend tests and 176 dashboard tests stayed green. Unit tests on either side alone
cannot see that class of defect, because each side is internally consistent.
This file is duplicated VERBATIM in both repos:
Both copies are sha256-pinned by a test in their own repo, so a change here fails a
build in the repo you edited and tells you to copy the file into the other one. Both
test files print the same expected hash — if the two hashes differ in review, the
The backend test drives the REAL services and validators and asserts their shapes
against this file. The dashboard test drives the REAL api client with a mocked fetch
and asserts the JSON body it actually sends against this file. Neither test restates
the shape, so there is exactly one place to change when the contract changes — and
changing it in one repo cannot silently pass in the other.
Contract changes are BREAKING unless both repos ship together. Bump `version`.

POST /policies/quote._note: Priced but not sold. The dashboard renders every response money field.

invariants: totalCost === premium. The platform fee is DEDUCTED OUT OF the premium (netPremium = premium - platformFee, the carrier's share); it is NOT added on top. payment.service charges against policy.premiumKES || policy.premium, so totalCost = premium + platformFee would overcharge every farmer by the fee.
totalCost is REQUIRED. It was once absent while the dashboard type declared it required: every quote screen rendered `undefined`.

POST /policies/purchase._note: Creates the policy PENDING and unpaid. It does NOT activate it and does NOT charge anyone — premium collection is POST /payments/initiate.

paymentInstructions._note: `amount` is a Prisma Decimal server-side and serialises to a STRING on the wire. Coerce with Number() before arithmetic or comparison.

invariants: The response is NOT a bare Policy. It is an envelope with the policy under `policy`. Typing it as a Policy silently loses paymentInstructions.amount, which is the exact amount POST /payments/initiate then needs.

POST /payments/initiate._note: MONEY PATH. Triggers the M-Pesa STK push that charges a farmer's phone.

invariants: `reference` is the POLICY id. Prisma DROPS undefined keys from a where clause, so a body missing it degraded the lookup into `findFirst({ where: { organizationId } })` — an arbitrary-row match on the money path.
`policyId` is accepted server-side as a back-compat alias only. New callers send `reference`.
`amount` is required and positive. The client must serialise it even when falsy, so a bad amount fails loudly as a validation error rather than as 'amount is required'.

response._note: `reference` here is the TRANSACTION reference (a fresh uuid), not the policy id that was sent in. The human-readable line is `instructions`, not `message`.
invariants: `keys` is the exact key set of the normal (fresh STK push) response. `optionalKeys` may be added on top of it by specific branches and NEVER replace a key in `keys`.
There is no `message`, and there never was. The dashboard typed one as REQUIRED, so any UI rendering it printed `undefined` on the money path immediately after charging a phone.

`alreadyPending: true` marks the replay-guard branch: a PENDING premium prompt for this policy is still fresh, so the existing transaction is returned and NO second STK push was sent. `orderId` and `provider` are read off the stored transaction there and may be null, so both are nullable client-side.
`simulated: true` + `warning` appear only under SIMULATE_PAYMENTS (sandbox). No money moved; the caller must be able to tell at a glance.

POST /determinations/:determinationId/se._note: NOT THE MONEY PATH, and that is the whole point. A Tier 1 (settlementMode = DETERMINATION) partner settles its farmer off-platform, off its own balance sheet, then tells us what it did. MicroCrop stores the claim, labels it PARTNER-ATTESTED and UNVERIFIED, and moves nothing: no Payout, no Transaction, no policy status change, no queue job.

invariants: `partnerReference` IS THE IDEMPOTENCY KEY, together with the determination id in the path. It is a BODY field, not an Idempotency-Key header, because it must be durable and queryable — an operator has to be able to ask 'have you already told us about M-Pesa ref QK73HG9XYZ?'. A client that generates a fresh key per attempt would post two attestations that the same money moved once.

`settledAmountMinor` is a decimal STRING of MINOR UNITS of `settlementCurrency` ('2250000' = KES 22,500.00). Never send a JSON number: it is an exact integer and a double loses precision at scale. The server rejects a number outright.
`settlementCurrency` MUST equal the policy's own currency. MicroCrop does not convert on this path — a mismatch is 400, never an FX conversion.
THERE IS NO USDC FIELD IN EITHER DIRECTION. The forbiddenFields above are not merely unused: sending one is a 400, so a client cannot believe it reported a USDC figure that was silently dropped.

`outcome` must agree with the amount: equal to what MicroCrop determined is owed => SETTLED_FULL; less => SETTLED_PARTIAL and `shortfallReason`; DECLINED => `declineReason` and settledAmountMinor '0'. More than the determined amount is refused.
A report is NEVER edited. A correction is a NEW request with a NEW `partnerReference` plus `supersedesReportId` naming the live report it replaces.

201 on a first recording, 200 with `replayed: true` on a replay of the same (determinationId, partnerReference). The stored row is returned verbatim on a replay; no second attestation is created, the AWAITING -> REPORTED transition does not re-run, and no webhook is re-emitted.

`settledByMicrocrop` and `verifiedByMicrocrop` are ALWAYS false here, and `verificationStatus` is always 'UNVERIFIED' (the Prisma enum has exactly one value). A UI must never render this as a MicroCrop settlement — show it as partner-attested and unverified, beside what MicroCrop determined, never merged into it.

`partnerSettlementStatus` is a REPORTING state (AWAITING_PARTNER_REPORT | REPORTED | OVERDUE), never a funding state. OVERDUE means we have no report by the due date; it does not mean MicroCrop owes anything.

Farmer._note: Every farmer endpoint returns the Prisma `Farmer` record verbatim, so the API field names ARE the Prisma column names. Three drifts have shipped off that: (1) the dashboard typed the phone `phone`, so every farmer phone rendered blank and the M-Pesa number never prefilled; (2) it typed the KYC rejection note `kycRejectionReason` while the column is `kycRejectedReason`, so a rejected farmer's reason never rendered; (3) it typed flat `plotsCount`/`policiesCount` while the list endpoint returns Prisma relation counts under `_count: { plots, policies }`, so both farmer-table columns were permanently blank.
Farmer._relationCountsNote: GET /farmers (list) includes `_count`. GET /farmers/:id (detail) includes the full `plots` and `policies` ARRAYS instead and returns no `_count` — so `_count` is optional client-side and must never be assumed present.
